site.name: aeroiq
site.summary: AeroIQ Fictional API monitoring and observability SaaS (Datadog / Vercel Observability-style). Pages - `index.html` — Overview dashboard. Left rail nav; top bar with org switcher, environment tabs (Production / Staging / Dev), time range (5m / 1h / 24h / 7d), search (⌘K), theme toggle, alert bell; four top KPIs (total requests / error rate / p95 / availability) with sparklines and period-over-period deltas; 24-card endpoint health grid (red cards first), each card with HTTP method + path + health dot + RPS / p95 / error rate; right alerts side panel with 8 active alerts and per-row assign / silence actions; bottom global p50 / p95 / p99 trend line chart. - `endpoint-detail.html` — Endpoint detail. Top: method + path + health badge + linked services + owner avatars; 6 KPIs (RPS / error rate / p50 / p95 / p99 / SLO status); three large trend charts (request volume, latency p50/p95/p99 three lines, error rate); error-grouping panel with status-code / client-version / region tabs; recent error sample table (5 rows including 502 Bad Gateway, 500, 429, 503); related traces list. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPIs (active / new today / mean response / MTTR); filter bar; 12-row alert

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full aeroiq system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The AeroIQ dashboard presents a visually dense but information-rich interface for API observability. While the visual hierarchy effectively highlights critical metrics (error rates, latency) and the endpoint detail view offers robust diagnostic tools, the system suffers from significant mobile usability flaws and broken interaction patterns in key controls. Critical navigation elements like the alert bell and user avatar are non-functional on mobile, and global filters (status, assignee) fail to respond on desktop, creating friction for incident management workflows.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of AeroIQ, focusing on the dashboard's information hierarchy, the drill-down flow to endpoint details, and the alert management workflow.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will start by validating the global controls (environment/time filters) on the Dashboard. It will then simulate an incident response workflow: identifying a failing endpoint from the grid, drilling down into its detail view to analyze error samples, and finally navigating to the Alerts center to manage notifications. The Service Map will be checked for navigational utility.
assumptions: The 'Logs', 'Integrations', and 'Settings' links in the sidebar are placeholders (#) and do not lead to functional pages.
The application is a static prototype; data updates may require page reloads or might be simulated via JS interactions.
The 'Service Map' relies on visual node interaction which may behave differently than standard list views.
risk_hotspots: Dashboard: Interaction between Environment tabs (Prod/Staging/Dev) and Time Range selectors.
Endpoint Detail: Readability of the 'Error breakdown' tabs and 'Recent error samples' table.
Alerts Page: Functionality of the multi-select filters (Severity, Status, Assignee).
Mobile Viewport: Sidebar navigation accessibility and tap target sizes (prescan flagged <44px targets).

phases.title: Dashboard Global Controls & Overview
phases.objective: Validate the primary entry point and global context switching.
key_checks: Click through Environment tabs (Production, Staging, Dev) to check for state changes.
Verify visibility and layout of the 4 KPI cards and the Endpoint Health grid.
exit_criteria: All global filters respond to clicks.
KPI cards and Endpoint grid are fully rendered.

phases.title: Incident Drill-Down Flow
phases.objective: Test the core user journey from high-level health to specific error diagnosis.
key_checks: Identify a 'Red' (unhealthy) endpoint card on the Dashboard (e.g., POST /v1/payments).
Click the endpoint card to navigate to `endpoint-detail.html`.
Analyze the Detail view: Check the 6 KPIs, Trend Charts, and Error Breakdown tabs.
Review the 'Recent error samples' table for readability and actionable data.
exit_criteria: Successful navigation from Dashboard to Detail view.
Detail view charts and tables are populated and legible.

phases.title: Alert Management Workflow
phases.objective: Evaluate how users monitor and resolve active incidents.
key_checks: From Dashboard, click 'view all' in the Active Alerts panel or the Alert bell icon.
On `alerts.html`, test the filter bar (Severity, Rule, Assignee, Status).
Attempt to interact with 'Assign' or 'Silence' actions on an alert row.
Check if clicking an alert row links back to the relevant endpoint detail.
exit_criteria: Filters apply correctly to the alert list.

phases.title: Inventory & Topology Exploration
phases.objective: Assess secondary navigation paths for system overview.
key_checks: Navigate to `endpoints.html`: Test sorting/filtering of the full endpoint list.
Navigate to `services.html`: Inspect the Service Map visualization.
Attempt to click a service node on the map to see if it links to details.
exit_criteria: Service map nodes are interactive or clearly informational.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Validate usability on smaller screens, addressing prescan warnings.
key_checks: Verify tap targets for Environment/Time filters (prescan noted <44px height).
Ensure tables (Endpoints/Alerts) handle horizontal overflow gracefully.
exit_criteria: Critical controls are usable despite small touch targets.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 HTML files provided in the site directory.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible filters, tabs, and navigation links. Interact with at least one 'Assign/Silence' action.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 (Dashboard) and Phase 3 (Alerts) checks on mobile viewport to verify layout shifts.

notes: Prescan identified multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings on the top bar filters; pay close attention to these during mobile testing.
The 'Logs' and 'Settings' pages appear to be stubs; do not spend steps attempting to debug them unless they unexpectedly load content.
Focus on the visual hierarchy of the 'Error breakdown' section in the detail view, as this is critical for debugging.

findings.user_goal: Access critical notifications and account settings while on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The Alert Bell (🔔) and User Avatar (👤) icons in the mobile header are non-interactive. Clicking them produces no dropdown, navigation, or visual feedback, effectively hiding critical alerts and account management features from mobile users.
findings.evidence: Steps 79-80 confirmed that clicking ux-19 (Alert Bell) and ux-20 (User Avatar) resulted in 'No obvious URL or visible-text change'. The reflection notes these as 'broken interaction pattern[s]'.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users, often engineers on-call, rely on quick access to alerts and settings. Dead-end icons create confusion and force users to navigate via the sidebar, which is less efficient and harder to reach on small screens.
findings.suggestion: Implement functional dropdowns or direct navigation links for the Alert Bell and User Avatar icons on mobile. Ensure they provide immediate visual feedback (e.g., opening a menu) upon interaction.

findings.user_goal: Filter alerts by status (Open/Resolved) or assignee to triage incidents efficiently.
findings.problem: The 'All status' and 'All assignees' filter dropdowns on the Alerts page are unresponsive. Clicking them fails to open the selection menu, preventing users from narrowing down the alert list.
findings.evidence: Step 13-18 trajectory notes: 'The click action on the All status dropdown... failed to produce any visible change; the dropdown menu did not open.' Same for 'All assignees'.
findings.why_it_matters: Filtering is core to managing high volumes of alerts. Broken filters force users to manually scan long lists, increasing cognitive load and slowing down incident response times.
findings.suggestion: Debug the event handlers for the status and assignee select inputs. Ensure they trigger the expected UI state change (opening the option list) and apply the filter to the data table.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the application using touch inputs on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Multiple primary navigation items and context toggles have tap targets smaller than the recommended 44px minimum height/width. The left rail nav items are ~39px wide, and environment toggles are ~28px high.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings persist across steps 6-79. Specifics: 'Left rail nav items... widths of only 39px', 'Environment toggle buttons... 91x28px'.
findings.why_it_matters: Sub-44px tap targets lead to frequent mis-taps ('fat finger' errors), causing frustration and accidental navigation. This is a significant accessibility barrier for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or hit-area size of all interactive elements in the mobile layout to meet the 44x44px minimum guideline. Use CSS `min-height` and `min-width` or invisible padding to expand touch targets without altering visual design if necessary.
findings.source_hint: index.html, endpoints.html (mobile viewport), selectors: ux-1 to ux-8, ux-10 to ux-12

findings.user_goal: Search for specific endpoints or alerts to investigate an issue.
findings.problem: The search input fields on the Dashboard and Alerts pages accept text but do not filter the visible results. Non-matching items remain visible after typing, indicating a lack of client-side filtering logic.
findings.evidence: Step 13-18 and 37-42 notes: 'The alert list did not filter; non-matching alerts... remain visible.' Step 73-78 showed the mobile endpoint search *did* work, highlighting inconsistency.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect immediate feedback when searching. A search box that doesn't filter feels broken and wastes time, leading users to abandon the feature and manually scan lists instead.
findings.suggestion: Implement real-time client-side filtering for the search inputs on the Dashboard and Alerts pages. If server-side filtering is required, provide a clear 'Search' button and loading state.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the interface using screen readers or assistive technologies.
findings.problem: Several form controls, including the 'Acme Cloud Org' selector and various filter dropdowns, lack explicit accessible labels (aria-label or visible label association).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in steps 25-30 and 55-60: 'Acme Cloud Org select input lacks an explicit accessible label', 'All services select inputs lack visible labels or aria-labels'.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear generic terms like 'combo box' or 'select menu' without context, making it difficult to understand what each control does. This violates WCAG guidelines.
findings.suggestion: Add descriptive `aria-label` attributes or associate visible `<label>` elements with all form inputs and select dropdowns to ensure they are announced correctly by assistive technologies.
findings.source_hint: index.html, endpoints.html, alerts.html, selectors: ux-9, ux-12
